subject: hagfish
title: A Hagfish Fires Snot That Grows 10,000 Times Bigger Around a Shark

scenes.text: This fish defends itself with snot. It beats sharks.
The hagfish is a long, eel-like fish with no jaws. When something bites it, it releases a tiny cloud of threads and mucus.
In water, that cloud expands up to ten thousand times its size in a few tenths of a second.
The slime is packed with coiled threads that unravel as the water rushes past them, then turn the water into a thick gel.
A predator that sucks in a mouthful gets gill filters clogged with goo. It has to let go or choke.
The hagfish slips away, while the shark is left fighting a mouthful of snot.

description:
A hagfish has no jaws, but when it is attacked it releases mucus and coiled threads that swell up to ten thousand times their size within a few tenths of a second.
Water flowing past is what unravels the threads and turns the water into a thick gel. Researchers have found it can clog the gills of suction-feeding predators.
Which animal would you least want to bite?
first_comment: A single tiny skein of hagfish thread goes from about a tenth of a millimeter to roughly ten centimeters when it unravels. Which animal defense should we cover next?
